fact: Cambridge CCAF 2025: 52.4% of Bitcoin mining electricity is now zero-emission (42.6% renewables, 9.8% nuclear). Coal fell from 36.6% in 2022 to 8.9%.
angle: Open with the accusation everyone repeats, then drop the numbers. Let the data flip the viewer's assumption.

topic: What one Bitcoin actually costs in electricity
fact: Post-halving, mining one BTC takes about 854,400 kWh at fleet-average efficiency, roughly 81 years of average US household use. Frontier machines at 9.5 J/TH cut that to about 115,000 kWh.
angle: Make it tangible. Compare to something everyone knows: a home, an EV, a city. The gap between average and frontier hardware is the real story.

topic: The machine that pays its own power bill
fact: Modern ASICs improved roughly 7x in energy efficiency over eight years, from about 65 J/TH to 9.5 J/TH at the frontier.
angle: Frame it as an engineering race most people never see. Show the hardware, talk about the physics of the squeeze.

topic: AI is hungry and miners know it
fact: AI data centers are projected at 40% of the roughly 1,000 TWh global data center footprint in 2026, up from 14% in 2024. Total data center demand could roughly double by 2030.
angle: Connect two worlds people keep separate: mining infrastructure and AI compute. Same skill, same power discipline.

fact: Around April 2028 the block reward drops from 3.125 to 1.5625 BTC, cutting daily issuance from about 450 to 225 BTC.
angle: Countdown content performs. Explain what halving means for the machines running right now, in plain words.

fact: Mining facilities recapture waste heat for greenhouses, district heating and agricultural drying, turning a cost into a second product.
angle: Show the pipes and the warmth. This is the most shareable story in mining: energy used twice.

fact: Miners in markets like ERCOT curtail within seconds when the grid peaks, acting as a flexible demand layer that grids increasingly pay for.
angle: Explain demand response like a story: when your city needs power, these machines step back. Nobody talks about this.

fact: The US holds about 37.9% of global hashrate, followed by China around 21% (mostly underground after the 2021 ban) and Kazakhstan around 13%.
angle: Map content. People love seeing the real geography of an invisible industry.

topic: The efficiency frontier vs the average
fact: Fleet-weighted ASIC efficiency is about 28 J/TH while frontier hydro-cooled machines reach 9.5 J/TH. Efficiency decides who survives a hashprice squeeze.
angle: Talk survival of the most efficient, not the biggest. A quiet lesson in any hardware business.

topic: Hashprice: the pulse of the industry
fact: Hashprice fell from about $55/PH/s/day in Q3 2025 to $28-34 by mid-2026, pushing machines above roughly 25-28 J/TH out of profit.
angle: Explain the metric that runs the whole industry in 30 seconds. Education that insiders will respect and reshare.

topic: Under one roof: mining and AI data centers
fact: The same requirements drive both: cheap firm power, serious cooling, 24/7 uptime. Facilities built for one increasingly serve the other.
angle: This is CyrusMiner's home turf. Show the infrastructure and let viewers draw the conclusion. Zero selling.

topic: Why cold places and hot machines go together
fact: Iceland and the Nordics use geothermal and hydro for baseload mining power, cooling with outside air most of the year.
angle: Travel-style content. The visual contrast of snow and servers is inherently shareable.

topic: The quiet rebirth after China's ban
fact: China's 2021 ban was expected to end its mining dominance. By 2025 Cambridge estimates put it back near 21% of global hashrate.
angle: A story of unintended consequences. Banning proof of work did not kill it, it moved it and made it more distributed.

fact: Nuclear now supplies about 9.8% of Bitcoin mining power, up from 4% in 2022, as miners sign long-term deals with reactors for firm clean power.
angle: The most surprising pairing in energy. Lead with the reactor image, explain the stable-load logic.

fact: Repurposed mining heat now warms greenhouses, apartment blocks and fish farms across Europe and North America.
angle: Same theme as heat reuse but told through people: the farmer, the building, the harvest. Human stories travel furthest.

topic: The numbers behind a mining facility day
fact: A mid-size facility can draw tens of megawatts around the clock. That is the scale of a small town, managed by a handful of engineers.
angle: A day-in-the-life angle. Scale shocks people when it is concrete.

topic: Why uptime is the whole game
fact: At current economics a machine offline is pure loss: every hour of downtime forfeits its share of the roughly 450 BTC issued daily.
angle: Frame the facility as an uptime culture: redundancy, monitoring, discipline. Professional pride content.

fact: Hydro-cooled and immersion-cooled ASICs run quieter, hotter and more efficiently, and can reach the 9.5 J/TH frontier class.
angle: Visual-first topic. Liquid and electronics together is inherently fascinating.

fact: After the April 2024 halving, hashprice compressed hard. Public miners sold over 32,000 BTC in Q1 2026, a single-quarter record.
angle: Explain the business cycle: margins compress, weak fleets shut down, difficulty adjusts, survivors strengthen.

topic: Difficulty does what it was designed to do
fact: Network difficulty has self-corrected for fifteen years: when hashrate falls, difficulty falls, and marginal machines switch back on.
angle: Nakamoto's thermostat. A design lesson that works even for viewers who do not care about crypto.

fact: Miners monetize flared gas and surplus hydro that would otherwise be wasted, at power prices down near $0.04/kWh where margins can reach roughly 49%.
angle: The economics of energy nobody wanted. A counterintuitive business story.

fact: Data centers overall are projected near 1,000 TWh in 2026. Bitcoin mining is estimated around 150 TWh, a fraction of what streaming and social platforms consume.
angle: Context check content. Polite, data-backed myth correction. Highly shareable in comment fights.

fact: One megawatt powers roughly 1,000 US homes. A serious mining hall runs many megawatts continuously.
angle: Unit literacy. Teach one number so well that viewers repeat it at dinner.

fact: In 2026 the binding constraint on both mining and AI is not chips or land, it is access to cheap firm power.
angle: A strategic take that positions infrastructure operators as the calm middle of a loud industry.

topic: Repair culture inside a mining farm
fact: Hashboards run at the edge of thermal limits. Skilled technicians diagnose, reball and revive boards daily to protect uptime.
angle: Hands and tools. Craftsmanship content earns trust like nothing else.

topic: Security budget after the next halving
fact: In 2028 daily issuance falls to about 225 BTC. The long-term security model shifts further toward transaction fees.
angle: A thoughtful, forward-looking piece. Signals depth without hype.

fact: Flexible load helps grids absorb renewable oversupply and stabilize frequency. Some regions now court miners for exactly this.
angle: Flip the narrative: not a burden, a tool. Backed by grid operator behavior.

fact: A single ASIC hashboard holds dozens of cutting-edge chips hashing trillions of operations per second at the edge of thermal design.
angle: Macro shots, slow pans. Let the hardware be the celebrity.

topic: Fifteen years of proof of work
fact: Bitcoin's network has run without a successful double-spend for fifteen years, secured purely by economic incentives and open competition.
angle: A milestone reflection. Sober, factual, confident.

fact: Dubai sits between cheap Gulf energy, global capital and a business-friendly AI and crypto regime, making it a natural hub for mining infrastructure and AI data centers.
angle: Home-field content. Show the city and the facility in one frame. Let location do the branding.
